summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for cough with bloody, mucopurulent tracheostomy secretions and post-viral symptoms. She had recently been treated for presumed viral bronchitis but continued to have dyspnea and malaise. A bronchoscopy revealed granulation tissue without active bleeding, and doxycycline was started to cover for possible bacterial infection. Her respiratory status improved, and she was weaned from supplemental oxygen to room air. She was discharged home with a seven-day course of oral doxycycline and follow-up arranged with her PCP and interventional pulmonology.
